note: The network-partition list element is allocated straight from the heap and its contents, including the interface_names member, are left uninitialized (no memset/calloc).

code: struct ddsi_config_networkpartition_listelem *new = if_common (cfgst, parent, cfgelem, sizeof(*new));
note: A NetworkPartition element from the crafted XML configuration causes this constructor to run; the returned struct still carries the uninitialized heap contents for interface_names.

Root cause: the initializer explicitly NULLs address_string, uc_addresses, asm_addresses, ssm_addresses and name, but never assigns new->interface_names = NULL, so interface_names stays as uninitialized heap garbage whenever the Interface attribute is omitted from the configuration.

The Interface cfgelem maps MEMBEROF(ddsi_config_networkpartition_listelem, interface_names) (line 652) and registers ff_free as its free function, so teardown will call ddsrt_free() on the interface_names pointer.
After the crafted configuration parses successfully (cfg->valid == 1), config teardown walks every configured element, including the NetworkPartition list, and frees all of its attributes.
For each ddsi_config_networkpartition_listelem in the networkPartitions list, its attribute table (which contains the Interface element) is recursively freed.
The Interface attribute's registered free function ff_free is invoked unconditionally, regardless of whether the Interface attribute was present in the configuration.
Sink: ddsrt_free() is called on *elem == new->interface_names, which is uninitialized heap garbage (not NULL, not a valid allocation), producing an invalid free / crash.
